answer_text:
Let

\[
a_p=\sum_{k=0}^{p}(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{(k+2)(k+4)}.
\]

First decompose the denominator:

\[
\frac1{(k+2)(k+4)}=\frac12\left(\frac1{k+2}-\frac1{k+4}\right).
\]

Hence

\[
a_p=\frac12\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+2}
-\frac12\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+4}.
\]

Now use

\[
\frac1{k+m}=\int_0^1 x^{k+m-1}\,dx,
\]

so that

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+m}
=\int_0^1 x^{m-1}(1-x)^p\,dx.
\]

For \(m=2\),

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+2}
=\int_0^1 x(1-x)^p\,dx
=\frac1{(p+1)(p+2)}.
\]

For \(m=4\),

\[
\sum_{k=0}^p(-1)^k\binom pk\frac1{k+4}
=\int_0^1 x^3(1-x)^p\,dx
=\frac{6}{(p+1)(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}.
\]

Therefore

\[
a_p=\frac12\left(\frac1{(p+1)(p+2)}
-\frac{6}{(p+1)(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}\right).
\]

Simplifying,

\[
a_p=\frac{p+6}{2(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}.
\]

Now decompose into telescoping terms:

\[
\frac{p+6}{(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)}
=\frac{2}{p+2}-\frac{3}{p+3}+\frac1{p+4},
\]

so

\[
a_p=\frac1{p+2}-\frac32\frac1{p+3}+\frac12\frac1{p+4}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
a_p=\left(\frac1{p+2}-\frac1{p+3}\right)
-\frac12\left(\frac1{p+3}-\frac1{p+4}\right).
\]

Thus the partial sum telescopes:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{p=0}^n a_p
&=\sum_{p=0}^n\left(\frac1{p+2}-\frac1{p+3}\right)
-\frac12\sum_{p=0}^n\left(\frac1{p+3}-\frac1{p+4}\right)\\
&=\left(\frac12-\frac1{n+3}\right)
-\frac12\left(\frac13-\frac1{n+4}\right)\\
&=\frac13-\frac1{n+3}+\frac1{2(n+4)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Taking \(n\to\infty\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{p=0}^n a_p=\frac13.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac13}
\]
